monthly_review.summary: This month shows a marked reduction in training volume and intensity compared to last month, with lower total km, fewer runs, slower average pace, and significantly less time spent in higher HR zones — indicating a deliberate or unintentional shift toward recovery or reduced load.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3+ time dropped from 45% of total HR distribution last month to just 13% this month — the largest categorical shift and strongest signal of reduced intensity.

goal_tracker.message: You need 21.1 more km across 6 sessions in the remaining 25 days to match last month’s volume — averaging 3.5 km per session, ideally distributed as 3x Zone 2 endurance runs (4–5 km) and 3x mixed-effort sessions including strides.

insights.title: Efficiency dip correlates with slower pacing and lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.1 m/sec per bpm this month; notably, your slowest recent run (10:07/km on 2026-05-05) had the lowest stride length (68.33m) and highest ground contact time (316ms), suggesting form breakdown at very low intensities.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold and VO2 max stimulus
insights.body: Zone 4+ time dropped from 19% last month (z4:15%, z5:4%) to just 1% this month (z4:1%, z5:0%), meaning no meaningful lactate threshold or VO2 max development occurred — critical for sustaining pace gains.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff evident in long run
insights.body: Your longest run (9.5 km, 10:55/km) showed cadence at 141 spm but stride length collapsed to 66.49m and ground contact spiked to 351ms — both outliers vs recent runs — indicating fatigue-related form deterioration.

insights.title: Low HR and high Z1 time suggest active recovery focus
insights.body: Z1 now accounts for 51% of HR time (vs 23% last month), and avg HR dropped 12 bpm — consistent with intentional recovery, especially given the 2.0 TE on the 2.8 km easy run (2026-05-05).

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run tomorrow at avg HR ≤138 bpm (use your 2026-04-29 HR of 143 as upper anchor), focusing on maintaining cadence ≥142 spm and stride length ≥85m.
recommendations.reason: Your last Zone 2 run (2026-04-29) hit 143 bpm and 88.65m stride — this preserves aerobic stimulus while rebuilding efficiency lost this month.

recommendations.action: Add 4 x 30-sec strides at 4:15–4:28/km pace post-run on your next 5 km session, walking 90 sec between, targeting cadence ≥152 spm and vertical oscillation <7.5 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your fastest recent pace was 428 sec/km (7:08/km) on 2026-04-29, but vertical oscillation was 8.2 cm — strides will reinforce neuromuscular efficiency without adding HR stress.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming easy run with a 3 km progressive run: 1 km @ 9:30/km (HR ~125), 1 km @ 8:30/km (HR ~133), 1 km @ 7:45/km (HR ~139), holding cadence ≥140 spm throughout.
recommendations.reason: This bridges Z1/Z2 into light Z3 stimulus (matching your 12% Z3 this month) and counters the 57 sec/km pace decline — your 2026-05-02 run at 8:50/km (530 sec/km) already shows capacity at that intensity.

weekly_focus.description: Focus on restoring cadence-stride coordination at varied paces while reintroducing controlled Z3 effort to reverse the sharp drop in higher-zone time and efficiency metrics.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 tempo with cadence target
4 km Z1/Z2 mixed with form drills
